q: Should memory ingest every conversational role, only user-authored statements, or a separately classified subset?
a: TypeScript accepts user|assistant|tool|system and stores role on every chunk (packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:3-13, packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:19-39).

q: Should extraction preserve unsupported/ambiguous input or discard it?
a: The TypeScript task processor has trivial-pattern and minimum-length gates; the Python simple reader falls back to a node when fine extraction is unparseable (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/task-processor.ts:7-18, packages/memos-core/src/ingest/task-processor.ts:410-466

q: Should assistant/tool material be evidence for preferences?
a: Python now removes assistant/tool/polluted sources before preference extraction (src/memos/mem_reader/source_filter.py:26-43, src/memos/mem_reader/source_filter.py:122-183; tests/mem_reader/test_source_filter.py:51-145).

q: Should the atomic unit be a raw event, extracted proposition, semantic chunk, entity/relation, or episode?
a: TypeScript stores paragraph chunks and mutable tasks; ChunkKind has only paragraph (packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:19-58).

q: Should raw evidence and derived summaries both persist?
a: TypeScript stores content and summary, and returns a source reference with timestamp, role, and session (packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:23-34; packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:71-85).

q: Should vectors live beside records, in a vector service, or be recomputable cache?
a: TypeScript stores dimensioned BLOBs in SQLite, deletes them by foreign-key cascade, and has no model/provider identity in the row (packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:70-75).

q: Should schema evolution be explicit/versioned or opportunistic at startup?
a: TypeScript performs ordered, catch-tolerant column probes and additive alterations (packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:99-123, packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:130-214).

q: Should short or trivial utterances be permanently dropped, stored raw but not indexed, or retained as episode context?
a: TypeScript drops/marks trivial content through fixed patterns and language-dependent length checks (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/task-processor.ts:7-18, packages/memos-core/src/ingest/task-processor.ts:410-466).

q: Should inactive duplicates be deleted or retained with lineage?
a: TypeScript marks old chunks duplicate/merged, keeps targets/reasons/history, and retrieves only active material (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:198-253; packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:631-634).

q: Should identical replay update recency/evidence, be ignored, or create a new observation?
a: TypeScript exact-hash handling retires/replaces through merge history; semantic candidates above 0.80 go to an LLM judge (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:151-182, packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:196-258).

q: When a new statement changes an old one, should the system merge text, supersede the old record, retain both, or ask?
a: The LLM returns DUPLICATE|UPDATE|NEW; UPDATE creates a new active chunk with merged summary and retires the target, while recording prior/new summaries (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:196-253).

q: Should conflict resolution be synchronous on write or asynchronous/versioned?
a: Python added scheduler version control and conflict-aware work later (tests/mem_scheduler/test_version_control.py:51-250), while issue #948 states the system previously lacked conflict-aware updates, causing duplicates and newer memories

q: Should retrieval be lexical, vector, graph, or hybrid?
a: TypeScript runs FTS, vector, pattern, and optional Hub sources, then reciprocal-rank fusion (packages/memos-core/src/recall/engine.ts:42-127; packages/memos-core/src/recall/rrf.ts:1-45).

q: Should ranking optimize relevance alone, relevance plus diversity, or relevance plus time?
a: TypeScript fuses ranks, MMR-reranks at lambda 0.7, applies a 14-day exponential half-life with a 0.3 floor multiplier, and then threshold-filters (packages/memos-core/src/recall/engine.ts:132-176; packages/memos-core/src/recall/mmr.ts:4-58; packages/memos-core/src/recall/recency.ts:1-25).

q: Should low absolute scores be compared to a global cutoff or to the best result in the current query?
a: TypeScript uses topScore × minScore × 0.3, then normalizes (packages/memos-core/src/recall/engine.ts:169-176).

q: Should session identity be a hard filter, a soft feature, or merely provenance?
a: TypeScript query schemas accept optional session/workspace/user/agent identity, while cross-session recall can be enabled by host integration (packages/memos-schema/src/index.ts:46-55).

q: Should the caller receive raw evidence, summaries, scores, provenance, or only injected prose?
a: TypeScript search exposes summary, excerpt, score, task/skill IDs, owner/origin, and source timestamp/role/session; prompt injection collapses hits into a formatted section (packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:71-105; packages/memos-schema/src/index.ts:90-97).

q: If summarization, embedding, or dedup fails, should ingestion fail closed, fail open, preserve raw memory, or report partial success?
a: The worker counts errors and continues per message; merge re-embedding failure is logged and processing continues (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:64-108, packages/memos-core/src/ingest/worker.ts:217-232).

q: Should low-confidence classification retry, abstain, or accept first pass?
a: Task boundaries below 0.65 confidence receive a second arbitration pass (packages/memos-core/src/ingest/task-processor.ts:196-216).

q: Should time affect record truth, retrieval priority, or both?
a: TypeScript preserves created/updated timestamps, task boundaries, merge history, and applies retrieval decay (packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:35-39; packages/memos-core/src/recall/recency.ts:12-25).

q: What ordering is assumed?
a: Messages carry timestamp, turn ID, session key, and seq; SQLite indexes (session_key, turn_id, seq) and (session_key, created_at, seq) (packages/memos-core/src/types.ts:5-13; packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:36-43).

q: What is idempotent?
a: Exact content hash within the TypeScript local store is treated as duplicate, but public MemoryEvent has no caller-supplied idempotency key (packages/memos-schema/src/index.ts:30-42; packages/memos-core/src/storage/sqlite.ts:487-492).

q: What enters memory?
a: Should memory ingest every conversational role, only user-authored statements, or a separately classified subset?

q: What is discarded?
a: Should short or trivial utterances be permanently dropped, stored raw but not indexed, or retained as episode context?
